chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch. 490: Gao Zhijian’s Fractured Past – Emperor or Madman?
chapter_meta_description: Gao Zhijian draws his impossible past in the dirt: an emperor killed at five, dying over and over. Chun Xiaoman and Zhao Wu struggle to make sense of a life that defies logic.
og_title: He Was an Emperor. He Was Murdered at Five. He’s Still Here. | DGYX Ch. 490
og_description: Gao Zhijian sketches a life of contradiction—royalty, murder, and silence. Chun Xiaoman can’t unravel it, and neither can you. Welcome to a different kind of Dao-Twisted horror.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Gao Zhijian draw instead of talking?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He has a severe stutter that worsens under emotional pressure; drawing lets him express layered, contradictory ideas that spoken language cannot handle.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Was Gao Zhijian actually a five-year-old emperor?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The novel leaves this deliberately ambiguous. Zhao Wu points out the logical impossibility, but Gao Zhijian’s terror and insistence suggest a fragmented truth—possibly from a different timeline, a false memory, or a Spirit-Blight’s influence.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Zhao Wu dismiss the emperor claim so quickly?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Because he’s applying real-world political logic. Great Liang has never had a child emperor that young, and Li Huowang couldn’t have killed a five-year-old version of Gao Zhijian when they’re similar in age. Zhao Wu is using common sense against a puzzle that likely has no common-sense answer.
